summary:
Atlalli is a Python data pipeline and statistical validation engine with an interactive suite to apply precedent-based detection and validation of long-term environmental trends in NASA earth observation time series. It uses NASA Giovanni monthly area-averaged time series (2000-2024) of precipitation (GPM), 2m air temperature (MERRA-2), and 0-10 cm soil moisture (GLDAS) to investigate climate dynamics in six contrasting regions (Chiapas, Morelos, Sonora, Zacatecas, the Sahel, and the South Amazon).
Natural variability inherent in raw environmental data may mask or simulate long-term change, possibly leading decision-makers astray. Atlalli addresses this by combining automatic data ingestion and metadata cataloging with formal statistical trend testing, empirical size (false-positive) simulations, and automated provenance and integrity checks. This allows for the production of transparent, statistically sound insights from complex satellite/reanalysis records rather than unsupported plots. This enables scientists, educators, and local populations to be confident in determining real-world geographic shifts in water and temperature availability and climate adaptation and resource and water management.
details:
What It Does and How It Works

Atlalli transforms raw satellite and reanalysis climate time series into verifiable statistical conclusions through a modular, three-stage architecture:

  1. Automated Data Ingestion and Cataloging (pipeline/): Scripts (ingest_giovanni.py and make_series_info.py) parse 18 raw NASA Giovanni CSV time series covering three key hydroclimatic variables—precipitation (precip), soil moisture (soil), and air temperature (temp)—across six geographic regions (chiapas, morelos, sonora, zacatecas, sahel, and south_amazon). The pipeline standardizes observations and metadata into structured artifacts (giovanni_observations.csv, series_info.csv, and giovanni_catalog.json).
  2. Statistical Trend Evaluation and Size Simulation (stats/): Core statistical modules (trends.py and analyze_giovanni.py) evaluate monotonic trends and statistical significance across each region-variable pair, exporting auditable results to giovanni_significance.csv. To ensure test reliability, simulate_size.py runs Monte Carlo simulations to verify empirical test size (Type I error control) under realistic time-series conditions.
  3. Interactive Web Atlas (app/web/): A static web atlas (HTML/CSS/JavaScript, live at atlalli.earth) whose explorer (explorar/) lets users select a region and variable to view the 2000–2024 series, its Sen’s slope trend with a 95% confidence band, and plain-language verdicts on whether observed changes are statistically meaningful or consistent with background noise.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Prevents Misinterpretation of Climate Data: By pairing trend estimates with formal significance testing and empirical size calibration, the tool protects users from drawing false conclusions from noisy or autocorrelated environmental records.
  • Cross-Regional Comparative Insight: Comparing arid/semi-arid zones (Sonora, Zacatecas, the Sahel) against humid tropical and temperate basins (Chiapas, Morelos, the South Amazon) highlights how hydroclimatic shifts manifest differently across ecosystems.
  • Reproducible Open Science: Every processed dataset, statistical verdict, and architectural choice is documented and reproducible from raw inputs, making the project immediately reusable by educators, researchers, and local planners.

Tools, Coding Languages and Data Resources

  • Programming Language and Ecosystem: Python, managed with reproducible dependency specifications (requirements.txt) and modular packages (pipeline, stats, app).
  • NASA Earth Observation Data (via NASA Giovanni): Monthly area-averaged time series (2000–2024) from GPM (GPM_3IMERGM v07, 0.1° precipitation), MERRA-2 (M2TMNXSLV v5.12.4, 0.5° × 0.625° 2m air temperature), and GLDAS Noah (GLDAS_NOAH025_M v2.1, 0.25° 0–10 cm soil moisture).
  • Quality Assurance and Engineering Practices: Automated test suites (stats/tests/) validating trend math (test_trends.py), Giovanni ingestion (test_giovanni.py), data provenance (test_provenance.py), report integrity (test_report_integrity.py), and application verdicts (test_app_verdicts.py, test_app_and_series_info.py), supported by Git version control and formal Architecture Decision Records (docs/ADR-001-trend-test.md).

How Our Project Is Creative

Rather than building a standard dashboard that simply plots raw CSV curves, Atlalli treats statistical validity and data provenance as core user-facing features. By embedding Monte Carlo size simulations (simulate_size.py), automated integrity tests, and plain-language "verdicts" directly into the workflow, it bridges the gap between rigorous climate econometrics/statistics and accessible interactive exploration.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Statistical Validity and False-Positive Control: Environmental time series often exhibit serial correlation and seasonality; we documented our methodological selection in ADR-001-trend-test.md and validated test calibration via simulate_size.py.
  • Climatic and Geographic Diversity: We deliberately selected six distinct regions spanning North America, South America, and West/Central Africa to stress-test the pipeline across contrasting precipitation and soil-moisture regimes.
  • End-to-End Provenance and Auditability: Dedicated provenance and report-integrity tests guarantee that every verdict displayed in the interface traces cleanly back to its original NASA Giovanni source file without silent corruption.
